description.short_caption: Erythematous skin lesion with surrounding demarcation and ruler for scale.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows an erythematous, irregularly shaped skin lesion on the thigh. The lesion is outlined with a marker, and a ruler is placed adjacent to it for scale, indicating a size of approximately 7 cm in its longest dimension. The lesion appears inflamed, with a red hue and slightly irregular borders. The label 'Timepoint B' suggests this is part of a time-sequenced observation.

description.short_caption: Two puncture wounds with surrounding erythema on the forearm.
description.detailed_description: The image shows the forearm of a patient with two puncture wounds approximately 2 cm apart. Both wounds exhibit surrounding erythema and mild ecchymosis. The wounds appear to have been sutured, and a measuring tape is placed adjacent to the site for scale. The surrounding skin shows no overt signs of necrosis or significant swelling.

description.short_caption: Erythematous lesion with central necrosis and surrounding induration on the thigh.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows a large, erythematous lesion on the thigh with a central area of necrosis and surrounding induration. The lesion is outlined with a marker, and a ruler is placed for size reference, indicating the lesion is approximately 5 cm in diameter. Labels 'A' and 'B' are marked on the image, likely for clinical reference. The lesion suggests a possible infectious or inflammatory process.

description.short_caption: Histopathology of a skin biopsy showing fungal elements.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of skin tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). Numerous darkly stained fungal elements, consistent with yeast forms, are visible within the dermis, surrounded by inflammatory cells. The fungal elements are highlighted in a circled area, suggesting their diagnostic significance. The background shows normal skin architecture with some disruption due to inflammation.

Case_10014/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Skin biopsy, hematoxylin and eosin stain.

description.short_caption: Skin biopsy with hematoxylin and eosin stain showing perivascular inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of skin stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The dermis contains a prominent perivascular inflammatory infiltrate, with lymphocytes and other mononuclear cells surrounding a blood vessel. The surrounding connective tissue appears pink and wavy, consistent with collagen fibers. No clear evidence of necrosis, granulomas, or microorganisms is visible in this image.
visible_findings: pink wavy collagen fibers in the dermis

Case_10014/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Gram stain of growth from blood culture.

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing gram-positive cocci in clusters from a blood culture.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of a blood culture specimen. Numerous gram-positive cocci are visible, arranged predominantly in clusters. The organisms are stained purple, consistent with their gram-positive nature. The background is relatively clear, with no significant debris or other cell types visible. This morphology is suggestive of staphylococcal species.
